scope: Proposition 2.1 (Preliminary mixing and rectangular doubling) of the manuscript “The canonical massive continuum limit of the two-dimensional O(3) model” (preprints/The-canonical-massive-continuum-limit-of-the-two-dimensional-O3-model-October-4-2026/massive-continuum-o3.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 215 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e75bfb353c2d3374), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 9. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are constants b0, C, c, p > 0 and η > 0 such that, with X(b) = C exp (4π − η)b  , b ≥ b0, (2.1) the following statements hold uniformly for all bond strengths 0 ≤ βe ≤ b, including zero. (i) On every unpinned rectangular torus whose sides are at least CX(b), and on every finite free subgraph of the square lattice, local Lipschitz observables F, G supported on A, A′ at distance d satisfy | Cov(F, G)| ≤ C(1 + b + |A| + |A′ | + d)p L(F)L(G)e−cd/X(b) . (2.2) In the homogeneous model the periodic infinite-plane limit exists and is unique. (ii) For each fixed aspect bound κ ≥ 1, the constants may be chosen so that, for even n, w with κ−1 ≤ n/w ≤ κ and min(n, w) ≥ CX(b), 0 ≤ 4 log Zb(n, w) − log Zb(2n, 2w) ≤ C(1 + b + n + w)p e−c min(n,w)/X(b) . (2.3)
